This Appeal Along With M.F.A.Crob Coming On For
Admission, This Day, The Court Delivered The
Following:
 Judgment
1. The insurer is in appeal challenging the finding that the Tribunal was incorrect in holding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident.
2. The insurer also contends that the amounts awarded by the Tribunal are excessive.
The claimant has also filed cross-objection seeking for enhancement of compensation.
3. The Tribunal on assessment of the evidence has awarded compensation of Rs.3,34,242/-.
4. It is the case of the insurer that there was a serious contradiction in the petition averments and the complaint which by itself indicated that the case putforth by the claimant was false.

It is also contended that as per the sketch which was produced it was clear that the claimant was trying to cross the road at a place where there was no zebra crossing and therefore, the attribution of negligence of just 20% was inadequate.
The Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs B A Raghavendra on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149362697/
3 5.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for claimant, however, contends that the attribution of negligence at 20% on the claimant was wholly improper.

Having regard to the fact that the chargesheet has been laid against the driver of the insured vehicle, it is also contended that the driver of the vehicle was never examined to establish any negligence.
Therefore, the finding regarding negligence is set aside.
6. It is not in dispute that an accident did occur between the tempo traveller which is insured by the insurer and the claimant.
It is also not in dispute that the accident occurred when the claimant was trying to cross the road.

The sketch which is produced indicates that the tempo traveller had a clear line of vision and therefore, even if the claimant was trying to cross the road at a place which was not earmarked for crossing, that would not allow the driver of the vehicle to hit the person crossing the road.
7. Furthermore, the driver of the tempo traveller was not examined to ascertain as to what was the negligent act of the claimant.

This coupled with the fact that the chargesheet was laid against the driver of the tempo traveller would lead to the inescapable decision that the driver of the tempo traveller would alone be responsible for the accident.

8. In this view of the matter, the appeal of the insurer as against negligence is dismissed and the appeal of the claimant insofar as it relates to the finding regarding negligence is allowed and it is held that the driver of the tempo traveller alone is responsible.
9. As far as compensation is concerned, it is contended that the determination of notional income is improper and the assessment of disability by the Tribunal is also improper.
It is also contended that the sums awarded under other heads are inadequate.
10. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.
The Doctor who treated the claimant has stated that the claimant has suffered 15% disability to the whole body.
Hence, the disability of claimant is taken at 15% to the whole body.
11. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.9,000/.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2017, would be Rs.11,000/-.

12. The argument that the loss of disability alone cannot be the criteria to ascertain the loss of earning capacity, in this case it cannot be accepted since it was the case of the claimant that he was executing sub contract works and in such an event if he has suffered 15% disability and that too as a result of fracture to the lumbar region, the loss of earning capacity should be taken at 15%.
Consequently, the argument of the insurer is rejected.
13. As the claimant was aged 36 years, a multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,97,000/- (Rs.11,000/- x 12 x '15' x 15%) towards 'loss of future income' .

4 14.

sentences.text: As a consequence, the amount of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.33,000/- (Rs.11,000/- X 3 months).
15. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
17. The compensation awarded under 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' is just and proper and is affirmed.

18. The sums awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.

19. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

1 . Pain and sufferings 40,000/- 50,000/-
 2. Loss of amenities - 50,000/-

 nourishment and  nutritious food  5. Loss of future 1,94,400/- 2,97,000/-
 earnings  6. Loss of income of 20,000/- 33,000/-
 family members of  claimant during laid-  up period

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,09,842/- as against Rs.3,34,242/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
21. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
